transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... my family and friends made me. They keep waving these bank papers at me, saying it proves nothing was taken. But paper doesn't mean anything. Like, the other day I found a receipt in my pocket and all the ink was just rubbed off. Completely blank. I found it in my heavy winter coat, the one I got from the thrift store.
Have you been feeling unusually high or euphoric lately?

High? No, I don't... I don't feel high. I'm just normal, you know? But speaking of high, I used to live on the fourth floor of this apartment building. The elevator was always broken, so I had to walk up all those stairs. It was a real workout. I'd carry my groceries up, and by the time I got to my door, I was sweating so much. I'd have to sit down for a good ten minutes before I could even put the milk away. And the neighbors, they were always playing this loud music, like, thump, thump, thump, all night long. It drove me crazy. I tried knocking on their door once, but they just ignored me. I don't know how people can be so inconsiderate, especially when the walls are so thin. You could hear everything. I could even hear the lady next door talking on the phone to her sister about her cat's stomach problems.
Do you believe someone stole money from you?

Stole it? Well, yeah. I mean, my family and friends keep saying those bank papers prove nothing was taken, but they're lying. It's been over a year, and I know for a fact they’re hiding my money. They use all these... these fake bills, and fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up. So I just have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth. 

You know, speaking of trips, my cousin was planning a trip to the lake. The lake is always so full of mosquitoes this time of year. I went a few summers ago and got bit up all over my ankles. I had to use this pink lotion... calamine, I think it's called? It smells real chalky. My grandma used to keep a bottle of it in her medicine cabinet right next to the bandages with the little stars on them. I always liked the star ones better than the plain brown ones, they just looked nicer. But anyway, yeah, they use all those trip plans and fundraisers and stuff to hide what they took from me.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is around?

Voices? No, I don't hear voices. Just the regular sounds, you know? Like the wind, or the cars outside. Speaking of cars, I used to have this old blue sedan. The muffler was completely shot, so it sounded like a tractor every time I started it up. It was so embarrassing, especially when I had to go to the grocery store. The grocery store near my old place always had the best apples, though. Honeycrisp, they were called. So sweet and crunchy. I'd buy a whole bag and just eat them on the porch. My porch had this wooden swing that squeaked every time you moved. I tried putting oil on it once, but it just made a mess on the floorboards and then the dog tracked it into the kitchen. He was a good dog, though. A golden retriever mix. He loved chasing those little green tennis balls.
How long have you believed that your family and friends are hiding your money?

Well, it started right around the time my income dropped... so, about a year and two months ago, I'd say. I remember because I was trying to figure out how to pay my light bill. The electric company, they send those envelopes with the little plastic windows, you know? And the paper is always that weird recycled gray color. I used to save those envelopes to write grocery lists on the back of them. My mom taught me that. She was always saving things, like butter tubs and glass jars. We had a whole cabinet just full of old jelly jars. The strawberry jelly was my favorite, the kind with the seeds still in it. You spread it on toast and the butter melts all into it... I used to eat that every morning before I stopped working. But yeah, it's been about a year and two months since they started hiding my money.
Have you ever had a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

Less sleep? No, I don't think so. I sleep pretty regular, mostly. I mean, unless it's too hot in the room. I can't sleep if it's hot. I used to have this little box fan, you know, the square ones? I kept it right by the bed, pointing right at my face. It had three speeds, but the button for the highest speed got stuck, so I had to use a butter knife to pry it back up if I wanted to turn it down. I don't know why I kept that knife in the bedroom. Oh, I used to eat peanut butter crackers in bed sometimes. Just the cheap kind in the orange wrapper. They always leave crumbs everywhere, though. You wake up and it feels like you're sleeping in sand. I went to the beach once when I was a kid and got sand all in my swimsuit, it was awful. It took days to wash it all out of my hair. But yeah, no, I just sleep normal, I guess. Nothing special about it.
Do you believe your family and friends are using special powers or technology to take or hide your money?

Special powers? No, no, they don't have powers or... or technology. They're just regular people. My brother works at a hardware store, actually. He's always wearing those heavy work boots, the tan ones that scuff up the linoleum. He came over once and tracked mud all the way from the front door to the kitchen sink. I had just mopped, too. I use that pine-scented cleaner, it comes in a big green jug. You only need a little capful, but it makes the whole house smell like a forest. I went camping in a forest once, up near the mountains. We slept in this tent that smelled like old canvas and mildew. It rained the whole weekend, so we just sat inside playing card games. Go Fish, mostly. The cards got all damp and stuck together. I hate when things get sticky like that. Like when you spill syrup on the table and don't wipe it up fast enough. But no, they aren't using anything special like that, just... regular ways, I guess.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or jumps from topic to topic?

Hard to follow? I... I don't think so. Nobody's ever said that to me. I mean, my mom used to tell me to slow down when I was little, but that was just because I'd get so excited about things. Like when the ice cream truck would come down our street. It played this song, I think it was "Turkey in the Straw," but it sounded all tinny and warped, you know? Like a music box that was running out of steam. I always got the kind shaped like a baseball glove with a gumball right in the middle for a baseball. The gumball was always rock hard, though. You could break a tooth on it if you weren't careful. My cousin actually chipped his front tooth on a piece of hard candy once at a parade. We used to sit on the curb and wait for them to throw the candy, but you had to be fast because the bigger kids would just scoop it all up. He had to go to the dentist, the one over by the old strip mall that shut down. They put a big plywood board over the window where the shoe store used to be. But no, nobody says I'm hard to understand or anything. I just talk normal.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Lost interest? I don't... no, I wouldn't say that. I still like the things I like. I watch my shows, you know. Mostly in the afternoons. The one with the judge, she has that wooden hammer... a gavel, right? She always bangs it so hard on the desk. I had a desk once, when I was in school, before I stopped going. It had all these carvings in the wood from the kids who sat there before me. Somebody carved a heart with an arrow through it, but the arrow was crooked. It looked more like a bent nail. My dad had a whole jar of rusty nails in the garage. He kept them in an old mayonnaise jar, the glass kind. You don't see glass jars for mayonnaise anymore, it's all plastic now. The plastic gets all greasy on the outside if you don't wipe it off. I hate when my hands get greasy. Like when you eat fried chicken at a picnic. We went to a picnic at the park by the lake, and the ducks kept trying to steal our bread. One of them actually bit my shoe. It didn't hurt, just felt weird. But no, I still enjoy things fine, I guess. Same as always.
Did this belief about your family and friends hiding your money come on all of a sudden?

All of a sudden? I... I don't really know if it was sudden. I don't keep track of the days very good. My grandma used to have this big calendar on her fridge, right next to the ice maker. It had pictures of kittens in baskets for every month. The August one was a little orange kitten tangled up in green yarn. My cat got into my yarn once. I was trying to make a scarf, just a plain blue one, because it gets so cold in the winter. The draft comes right under the front door. We tried putting one of those heavy snake things, you know, the fabric tubes filled with beans or whatever, to stop the wind. But a mouse chewed a hole in it. Tiny little dry beans spilled everywhere on the rug. The vacuum couldn't even pick them all up. It's one of those old vacuums with the big cloth bag that puffs up like a balloon when you turn it on. It sounds like an airplane taking off, it's so loud. My ears ring if I use it too long. So... no, I don't know exactly when it started with the money. I just know they're doing it.
Do you believe your family and friends have done something impossible or supernatural to hide your money?

Supernatural? I... no, I don't think it's magic or ghosts or anything like that. That's just silly. People don't do magic. They just... they hide things. Like how squirrels hide their acorns before the snow comes. I saw a squirrel bury a whole peanut in its shell right in the middle of Mrs. Gable's flower bed once. She had these big, bright yellow tulips. They only bloomed for a couple of weeks in the spring, and then the petals would just fall off, all over the sidewalk. They looked like little yellow boats when it rained and the water rushed down the gutter. I made a paper boat once out of a newspaper, the Sunday edition with the color comics. I liked the one with the big orange cat who loved lasagna. We had lasagna for dinner last week, but the edges got all burnt and crispy because the oven gets too hot on the left side. You have to turn the pan halfway through if you want it to bake even. The timer on the stove doesn't buzz anymore, it just makes this weak little clicking sound. So you really have to watch the clock on the wall. The clock with the big red second hand that sweeps around... but no, it's not impossible what they're doing with my money. They're just doing it.
Has your way of talking been like this for most of your life, or is it something that started around the time you began believing your money was being hidden?

My way of talking? I don't... I mean, this is just how I talk. I've always talked like this, I think. My mom used to say I could talk the ears off a brass monkey. We had a little brass monkey statue on the bookshelf in the hallway. It was supposed to be one of those "hear no evil, see no evil" things, but it was just the one monkey covering his eyes. His little brass fingers were all tarnished and green from people touching him. I tried to polish him once with that silver cream in the pink plastic tub, but it smelled so bad, like rotten eggs and chemicals. It made my eyes water. I had to open the window in the hall, the one with the screen that had a hole in it where a grasshopper got stuck. It was a huge green grasshopper, with those long, spiky legs. They make that weird clicking noise when they fly, like a tiny little motor. My brother caught one in a jar and fed it blades of grass, but it died anyway. He buried it in the backyard under the old oak tree. That tree dropped so many leaves in the fall, we'd rake them into massive piles and jump in them. They smelled so dusty and earthy. But yeah, I don't know, my talking hasn't changed. Just always been me.
Do you ever feel that someone can put thoughts into your mind?

Put thoughts in my mind? No, nobody can do that. That's... that's like science fiction or something. Like those movies with the aliens that have the big giant heads and the silver suits. We watched one of those on a Friday night once. My dad used to make popcorn in this big metal pot on the stove, not the microwave kind. You had to shake the pot back and forth, back and forth, so the kernels wouldn't burn on the bottom. It sounded like a maraca. Shake, shake, pop, pop. We'd pour real melted butter over it, and it would make the popcorn shrink a little bit and get all soggy, but it tasted so good. I got a kernel stuck in my teeth once, way in the back, and it hurt for three days. I tried using a toothpick, but it just pushed it in deeper. Toothpicks always splinter anyway if you bite on them too hard. My uncle used to chew on toothpicks all the time after dinner. He had this plaid shirt he wore every single Sunday, red and black squares. It was flannel, and it was so soft from being washed a million times. The elbows were practically worn through. So, no, nobody's putting thoughts in my head. My thoughts are just mine.
Did your belief that they were hiding your money begin within a period of less than two weeks?

Less than two weeks? I... I don't really know how fast it started. Time is kind of funny like that. Sometimes a week feels like a whole year, you know? Like when it rains every single day. We had a week like that last April. Just gray and pouring, non-stop. The gutters overflowed and made this huge puddle at the bottom of the driveway. It looked like a little lake. A pair of ducks actually landed in it one morning! A boy and a girl duck. The boy duck had that shiny green head that looks like velvet when the sun hits it. They were just paddling around in the driveway puddle, dipping their heads underwater to look for bugs or whatever ducks eat. I tried to throw them some bread, but my neighbor Mrs. Higgins yelled at me. She said bread is bad for ducks, it makes their stomachs swell up. She's always yelling about something, Mrs. Higgins. She has this little white dog, a poodle mix I think, that barks at every single car that drives by. It's a high-pitched, yappy bark that goes right through your ears. She ties him to the front porch with a long blue leash, and he just runs back and forth, back and forth, tangling himself around the porch railing. He got so tangled once he was practically hanging there, and she had to come out with scissors to cut the leash. It was a brand new leash, too. But... yeah, I'm not sure how long it took for the money thing to start. It just sort of... happened.
Have you had less facial expression or less emotion in your voice than you used to?

Less emotion? I don't think so. I mean, my face is just my face, right? I guess sometimes people say I look tired, but that's just because I don't sleep well when it's hot out. The air conditioner in my window is so loud. It rattles. It sounds like a box of rocks in a washing machine. I tried putting a folded-up piece of cardboard under the corner to make it stop, but it didn't really work. The cardboard was from a pizza box. Pepperoni and mushroom. The mushrooms get all wrinkly and black when they bake them, they don't even look like mushrooms anymore. My cousin grows mushrooms in her basement. It's so dark and damp down there, it smells like wet dirt. She has these big plastic bags filled with sawdust and spores, and they just sprout right out of the plastic. It's kind of creepy, honestly. Like little alien fingers pushing out. She gave me some to cook once, but I threw them away because I was scared they were poisonous. You hear stories about people eating the wrong mushroom and just dropping dead in the woods. So, yeah, no, my face is fine, my voice is fine.
Aside from the money, do you believe anyone is trying to harm you or plot against you?

Harm me? No, nobody is trying to hurt me or anything like that. It's just the money they're after. People get so crazy about money, you know? Like my aunt, she used to buy those scratch-off lottery tickets every single Tuesday. She said Tuesday was her lucky day because she was born on a Tuesday. She'd buy five of the shiny gold ones, the ones that cost five dollars each, and sit at her kitchen table scratching them with a special silver coin. It was a quarter from 1976, the Bicentennial one with the drummer boy on the back. She said the regular eagle quarters didn't work. One time she actually won fifty bucks, and she went right out and bought a huge ham for Sunday dinner. It was one of those spiral-cut hams with the sweet glaze on the outside, and it came with a little packet of extra sugar to melt over it. We ate ham sandwiches for a week after that. White bread, yellow mustard, and a slice of American cheese. The cheese always sticks to the roof of your mouth if you don't drink enough water with it. I prefer Swiss cheese, honestly. The holes in it are so funny. I used to look through them like a telescope when I was a kid. So, no, nobody's plotting to hurt me, just the money thing.
Have there ever been times when, besides the money belief, you were very confused or your behavior got so disorganized that other people were worried about you?

Confused? No, I don't think I've ever been confused like that. I mean, I keep my house clean, I do my own grocery shopping... well, usually on Thursdays. Thursday mornings are the best time to go because they restock the produce aisle. The apples are always so shiny on Thursdays. I like the green ones, Granny Smiths, they're so sour they make your jaw tingle. My grandma used to bake pies with them. She had this old rolling pin made of solid cherry wood, it was so heavy I could barely lift it when I was little. She'd roll the dough out so thin you could almost see through it, and then she'd cut it into strips to make a lattice pattern on top of the pie. She always burnt the edges just a tiny bit, but I liked it that way. The burnt crust tasted like caramel. She kept her flour in this big ceramic jar shaped like a fat chef. The chef had a little painted mustache that was chipping off. So no, nobody's ever been worried about me being disorganized or anything. I'm perfectly fine.
Do you ever feel that other people can hear your thoughts?

Hear my thoughts? No, that's impossible, isn't it? I mean, thoughts are inside your head. It's like... like when you put something in a drawer and lock it. I have this little wooden box on my dresser, actually. It's got a tiny brass lock on it, the kind that looks like a heart. I lost the key years ago, though. It was on a red ribbon, a really thin velvet ribbon that I used to tie around my wrist. I think I left it at a diner once. It was this place off the highway that served breakfast all day, and they had these booths with red vinyl seats that squeaked every time you moved. I ordered pancakes, but they came out all burnt on the bottom. The waitress had bright blue eyeshadow, like, really bright, almost neon. She kept calling me "hon," which I didn't mind, but she smelled strongly of peppermint. Like she'd eaten a whole bag of those little red and white striped candies. I tried making those candies once, but the sugar got too hot and ruined my favorite saucepan. It was a copper-bottom pan, really expensive. So, no, nobody can hear what I'm thinking.
When you say they are hiding your money, do you believe they physically took it or moved it in ordinary ways?

Well, it's not like they just put it in a different account. I came in here because my family and friends, they keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken. But those papers are just... they're just paper. You can print anything on paper. Like those flyers they put under your windshield wipers at the grocery store. I always get them when I park near the cart return. Last week it was a flyer for a car wash, but the ink was all smudged because it had rained. It rained so hard on Tuesday, the gutters were overflowing and making this loud rushing sound. It sounded like a waterfall right outside my bedroom window. I used to love waterfalls when I was little. We went to this one park that had a huge waterfall, and the mist would get all over your face and make your hair frizzy. My mom used to carry this little pink comb in her purse to fix my hair, but it never worked. The comb had a tooth missing right in the middle. Anyway, for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money. They're using all these things to cover it up—like paying bills, or these fundraisers they talk about, or planning trips. It's all just a cover-up for where the money really went. So I just have to keep confronting them, you know? I have to keep asking them until they finally tell the truth. They think they can just distract me with all this talk about trips. I went on a trip to the beach once, and I found a perfect sand dollar, but it broke in my pocket on the way home. It just crumbled into dust.

patient.answer: Special powers? No, no, they don't have powers or... or technology. They're just regular people. My brother works at a hardware store, actually. He's always wearing those heavy work boots, the tan ones that scuff up the linoleum. He came over once and tracked mud all the way from the front door to the kitchen sink. I had just mopped, too. I use that pine-scented cleaner, it comes in a big green jug. You only need a little capful, but it makes the whole house smell like a forest. I went camping in a forest once, up near the mountains. We slept in this tent that smelled like old canvas and mildew. It rained the whole weekend, so we just sat inside playing card games. Go Fish, mostly. The cards got all damp and stuck together. I hate when things get sticky like that. Like when you spill syrup on the table and don't wipe it up fast enough. But no, they aren't using anything special like that, just... regular ways, I guess.

inference.note: F31.2 ruled out by repeated denial of elevated mood, decreased need for sleep, or increased energy; persistent non-bizarre persecutory delusion >1 year without hallucinations supports F22 most strongly, though schizophrenia-spectrum disorders remain in differential due to marked circumstantial/tangential thought process.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms are accompanied by prominent thought disorder/disorganized speech, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from persistent delusional disorder or acute polymorphic psychosis.
doctor.question: Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or jumps from topic to topic?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized speech (jumping from topic to topic or being hard to follow), which is a symptom of schizophrenia or other psychotic disorders (e.g., formal thought disorder/derailment). This is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile (Delusions, Additional Requirement 1, Functional Impairment, Duration).

patient.answer: Hard to follow? I... I don't think so. Nobody's ever said that to me. I mean, my mom used to tell me to slow down when I was little, but that was just because I'd get so excited about things. Like when the ice cream truck would come down our street. It played this song, I think it was "Turkey in the Straw," but it sounded all tinny and warped, you know? Like a music box that was running out of steam. I always got the kind shaped like a baseball glove with a gumball right in the middle for a baseball. The gumball was always rock hard, though. You could break a tooth on it if you weren't careful. My cousin actually chipped his front tooth on a piece of hard candy once at a parade. We used to sit on the curb and wait for them to throw the candy, but you had to be fast because the bigger kids would just scoop it all up. He had to go to the dentist, the one over by the old strip mall that shut down. They put a big plywood board over the window where the shoe store used to be. But no, nobody says I'm hard to understand or anything. I just talk normal.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are persistent negative symptoms, which would support schizophrenia (F20.0) over delusional disorder (F22) or acute polymorphic psychotic disorder (F23.3).
doctor.question: Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities (anhedonia), which is a symptom of depression. This is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: Lost interest? I don't... no, I wouldn't say that. I still like the things I like. I watch my shows, you know. Mostly in the afternoons. The one with the judge, she has that wooden hammer... a gavel, right? She always bangs it so hard on the desk. I had a desk once, when I was in school, before I stopped going. It had all these carvings in the wood from the kids who sat there before me. Somebody carved a heart with an arrow through it, but the arrow was crooked. It looked more like a bent nail. My dad had a whole jar of rusty nails in the garage. He kept them in an old mayonnaise jar, the glass kind. You don't see glass jars for mayonnaise anymore, it's all plastic now. The plastic gets all greasy on the outside if you don't wipe it off. I hate when my hands get greasy. Like when you eat fried chicken at a picnic. We went to a picnic at the park by the lake, and the ducks kept trying to steal our bread. One of them actually bit my shoe. It didn't hurt, just felt weird. But no, I still enjoy things fine, I guess. Same as always.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms began suddenly, which would help distinguish acute/transient psychotic disorder from more persistent delusional or schizophrenic illness.
doctor.question: Did this belief about your family and friends hiding your money come on all of a sudden?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the onset of the delusion (whether it came on suddenly). The provided symptom profiles do not include information about the onset of the delusion, only its duration, manifestation, and impact on functioning.

patient.answer: All of a sudden? I... I don't really know if it was sudden. I don't keep track of the days very good. My grandma used to have this big calendar on her fridge, right next to the ice maker. It had pictures of kittens in baskets for every month. The August one was a little orange kitten tangled up in green yarn. My cat got into my yarn once. I was trying to make a scarf, just a plain blue one, because it gets so cold in the winter. The draft comes right under the front door. We tried putting one of those heavy snake things, you know, the fabric tubes filled with beans or whatever, to stop the wind. But a mouse chewed a hole in it. Tiny little dry beans spilled everywhere on the rug. The vacuum couldn't even pick them all up. It's one of those old vacuums with the big cloth bag that puffs up like a balloon when you turn it on. It sounds like an airplane taking off, it's so loud. My ears ring if I use it too long. So... no, I don't know exactly when it started with the money. I just know they're doing it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is bizarre/impossible versus a plausible persecutory theft belief, which best separates schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis from persistent delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Do you believe your family and friends have done something impossible or supernatural to hide your money?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient believes the family and friends have done something impossible or supernatural to hide the money (which assesses for bizarre delusions). The symptom profile describes the delusion (S019) but does not specifically mention whether the delusion involves impossible/supernatural elements (the profile just says they use bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up). Therefore, there is no specific item in the profile that directly answers if it is impossible or supernatural.

patient.answer: Supernatural? I... no, I don't think it's magic or ghosts or anything like that. That's just silly. People don't do magic. They just... they hide things. Like how squirrels hide their acorns before the snow comes. I saw a squirrel bury a whole peanut in its shell right in the middle of Mrs. Gable's flower bed once. She had these big, bright yellow tulips. They only bloomed for a couple of weeks in the spring, and then the petals would just fall off, all over the sidewalk. They looked like little yellow boats when it rained and the water rushed down the gutter. I made a paper boat once out of a newspaper, the Sunday edition with the color comics. I liked the one with the big orange cat who loved lasagna. We had lasagna for dinner last week, but the edges got all burnt and crispy because the oven gets too hot on the left side. You have to turn the pan halfway through if you want it to bake even. The timer on the stove doesn't buzz anymore, it just makes this weak little clicking sound. So you really have to watch the clock on the wall. The clock with the big red second hand that sweeps around... but no, it's not impossible what they're doing with my money. They're just doing it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the prominent derailment/tangentiality is a longstanding trait or a new change, to distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder and acute psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: Has your way of talking been like this for most of your life, or is it something that started around the time you began believing your money was being hidden?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's disorganized or tangential speech pattern and whether it has been present for most of her life or started recently. This is assessing for disorganized speech or thought disorder, which is not covered in the provided symptom profiles (Delusions, Additional Requirement 1, Functional Impairment, Duration).

patient.answer: My way of talking? I don't... I mean, this is just how I talk. I've always talked like this, I think. My mom used to say I could talk the ears off a brass monkey. We had a little brass monkey statue on the bookshelf in the hallway. It was supposed to be one of those "hear no evil, see no evil" things, but it was just the one monkey covering his eyes. His little brass fingers were all tarnished and green from people touching him. I tried to polish him once with that silver cream in the pink plastic tub, but it smelled so bad, like rotten eggs and chemicals. It made my eyes water. I had to open the window in the hall, the one with the screen that had a hole in it where a grasshopper got stuck. It was a huge green grasshopper, with those long, spiky legs. They make that weird clicking noise when they fly, like a tiny little motor. My brother caught one in a jar and fed it blades of grass, but it died anyway. He buried it in the backyard under the old oak tree. That tree dropped so many leaves in the fall, we'd rake them into massive piles and jump in them. They smelled so dusty and earthy. But yeah, I don't know, my talking hasn't changed. Just always been me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is accompanied by bizarre passivity/control phenomena or thought interference, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder or acute psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: Do you ever feel that someone can put thoughts into your mind?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought insertion (a symptom of schizophrenia), which is not present in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: Put thoughts in my mind? No, nobody can do that. That's... that's like science fiction or something. Like those movies with the aliens that have the big giant heads and the silver suits. We watched one of those on a Friday night once. My dad used to make popcorn in this big metal pot on the stove, not the microwave kind. You had to shake the pot back and forth, back and forth, so the kernels wouldn't burn on the bottom. It sounded like a maraca. Shake, shake, pop, pop. We'd pour real melted butter over it, and it would make the popcorn shrink a little bit and get all soggy, but it tasted so good. I got a kernel stuck in my teeth once, way in the back, and it hurt for three days. I tried using a toothpick, but it just pushed it in deeper. Toothpicks always splinter anyway if you bite on them too hard. My uncle used to chew on toothpicks all the time after dinner. He had this plaid shirt he wore every single Sunday, red and black squares. It was flannel, and it was so soft from being washed a million times. The elbows were practically worn through. So, no, nobody's putting thoughts in my head. My thoughts are just mine.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a clear acute onset of psychotic symptoms, which best distinguishes acute polymorphic psychotic disorder from a more chronic delusional or schizophrenic disorder.
doctor.question: Did your belief that they were hiding your money begin within a period of less than two weeks?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the onset of the delusion (whether it started within a period of less than two weeks). The symptom profile includes duration (1 year and 2 months), but it does not specify the rapidity of onset (e.g., acute onset within 2 weeks).

patient.answer: Less than two weeks? I... I don't really know how fast it started. Time is kind of funny like that. Sometimes a week feels like a whole year, you know? Like when it rains every single day. We had a week like that last April. Just gray and pouring, non-stop. The gutters overflowed and made this huge puddle at the bottom of the driveway. It looked like a little lake. A pair of ducks actually landed in it one morning! A boy and a girl duck. The boy duck had that shiny green head that looks like velvet when the sun hits it. They were just paddling around in the driveway puddle, dipping their heads underwater to look for bugs or whatever ducks eat. I tried to throw them some bread, but my neighbor Mrs. Higgins yelled at me. She said bread is bad for ducks, it makes their stomachs swell up. She's always yelling about something, Mrs. Higgins. She has this little white dog, a poodle mix I think, that barks at every single car that drives by. It's a high-pitched, yappy bark that goes right through your ears. She ties him to the front porch with a long blue leash, and he just runs back and forth, back and forth, tangling himself around the porch railing. He got so tangled once he was practically hanging there, and she had to come out with scissors to cut the leash. It was a brand new leash, too. But... yeah, I'm not sure how long it took for the money thing to start. It just sort of... happened.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms, which would support schizophrenia over delusional disorder or acute psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: Have you had less facial expression or less emotion in your voice than you used to?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about flat affect (less facial expression or less emotion in the voice), which is a negative symptom of schizophrenia. This symptom is not present in my profile.

patient.answer: Less emotion? I don't think so. I mean, my face is just my face, right? I guess sometimes people say I look tired, but that's just because I don't sleep well when it's hot out. The air conditioner in my window is so loud. It rattles. It sounds like a box of rocks in a washing machine. I tried putting a folded-up piece of cardboard under the corner to make it stop, but it didn't really work. The cardboard was from a pizza box. Pepperoni and mushroom. The mushrooms get all wrinkly and black when they bake them, they don't even look like mushrooms anymore. My cousin grows mushrooms in her basement. It's so dark and damp down there, it smells like wet dirt. She has these big plastic bags filled with sawdust and spores, and they just sprout right out of the plastic. It's kind of creepy, honestly. Like little alien fingers pushing out. She gave me some to cook once, but I threw them away because I was scared they were poisonous. You hear stories about people eating the wrong mushroom and just dropping dead in the woods. So, yeah, no, my face is fine, my voice is fine.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a persistent non-bizarre delusional belief in the absence of Schneiderian first-rank/passivity symptoms, helping distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia or acute polymorphic psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: Aside from the money, do you believe anyone is trying to harm you or plot against you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about persecutory delusions (believing someone is trying to harm or plot against the patient). My symptom profile only includes delusions about people hiding my money, and does not include any other types of delusions such as persecutory ones.

patient.answer: Harm me? No, nobody is trying to hurt me or anything like that. It's just the money they're after. People get so crazy about money, you know? Like my aunt, she used to buy those scratch-off lottery tickets every single Tuesday. She said Tuesday was her lucky day because she was born on a Tuesday. She'd buy five of the shiny gold ones, the ones that cost five dollars each, and sit at her kitchen table scratching them with a special silver coin. It was a quarter from 1976, the Bicentennial one with the drummer boy on the back. She said the regular eagle quarters didn't work. One time she actually won fifty bucks, and she went right out and bought a huge ham for Sunday dinner. It was one of those spiral-cut hams with the sweet glaze on the outside, and it came with a little packet of extra sugar to melt over it. We ate ham sandwiches for a week after that. White bread, yellow mustard, and a slice of American cheese. The cheese always sticks to the roof of your mouth if you don't drink enough water with it. I prefer Swiss cheese, honestly. The holes in it are so funny. I used to look through them like a telescope when I was a kid. So, no, nobody's plotting to hurt me, just the money thing.

inference.note: Sustained non-bizarre persecutory delusion >1 year with preserved affect/interests and no hallucinations, thought insertion, negative symptoms, or broader persecutory system outside the money theme makes F22 more likely; F23.3 ruled out by chronic duration >3 months.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a sustained period of prominent hallucinations or disorganized speech/behavior in addition to the delusion, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have there ever been times when, besides the money belief, you were very confused or your behavior got so disorganized that other people were worried about you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about periods of confusion or disorganized behavior (symptoms of disorganized speech or behavior often seen in schizophrenia or delirium). My symptom profile does not include any information about disorganized behavior or confusion, only delusions, functioning, and duration.

patient.answer: Confused? No, I don't think I've ever been confused like that. I mean, I keep my house clean, I do my own grocery shopping... well, usually on Thursdays. Thursday mornings are the best time to go because they restock the produce aisle. The apples are always so shiny on Thursdays. I like the green ones, Granny Smiths, they're so sour they make your jaw tingle. My grandma used to bake pies with them. She had this old rolling pin made of solid cherry wood, it was so heavy I could barely lift it when I was little. She'd roll the dough out so thin you could almost see through it, and then she'd cut it into strips to make a lattice pattern on top of the pie. She always burnt the edges just a tiny bit, but I liked it that way. The burnt crust tasted like caramel. She kept her flour in this big ceramic jar shaped like a fat chef. The chef had a little painted mustache that was chipping off. So no, nobody's ever been worried about me being disorganized or anything. I'm perfectly fine.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are persistent first-rank psychotic symptoms outside the non-bizarre money delusion, especially thought broadcasting, to distinguish schizophrenia (F20.0) from delusional disorder (F22).
doctor.question: Do you ever feel that other people can hear your thoughts?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought broadcasting (feeling that others can hear one's thoughts), which is a symptom of schizophrenia or other psychotic disorders. This is not covered by any of the items in the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer: Hear my thoughts? No, that's impossible, isn't it? I mean, thoughts are inside your head. It's like... like when you put something in a drawer and lock it. I have this little wooden box on my dresser, actually. It's got a tiny brass lock on it, the kind that looks like a heart. I lost the key years ago, though. It was on a red ribbon, a really thin velvet ribbon that I used to tie around my wrist. I think I left it at a diner once. It was this place off the highway that served breakfast all day, and they had these booths with red vinyl seats that squeaked every time you moved. I ordered pancakes, but they came out all burnt on the bottom. The waitress had bright blue eyeshadow, like, really bright, almost neon. She kept calling me "hon," which I didn't mind, but she smelled strongly of peppermint. Like she'd eaten a whole bag of those little red and white striped candies. I tried making those candies once, but the sugar got too hot and ruined my favorite saucepan. It was a copper-bottom pan, really expensive. So, no, nobody can hear what I'm thinking.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is bizarre or non-bizarre to distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia.
doctor.question: When you say they are hiding your money, do you believe they physically took it or moved it in ordinary ways?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the mechanics of the patient's belief regarding the hidden money ('do you believe they physically took it or moved it in ordinary ways?'). This directly addresses the nature of the patient's delusion, which is the core symptom under 'Delusions' (S019).

patient.answer: Well, it's not like they just put it in a different account. I came in here because my family and friends, they keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken. But those papers are just... they're just paper. You can print anything on paper. Like those flyers they put under your windshield wipers at the grocery store. I always get them when I park near the cart return. Last week it was a flyer for a car wash, but the ink was all smudged because it had rained. It rained so hard on Tuesday, the gutters were overflowing and making this loud rushing sound. It sounded like a waterfall right outside my bedroom window. I used to love waterfalls when I was little. We went to this one park that had a huge waterfall, and the mist would get all over your face and make your hair frizzy. My mom used to carry this little pink comb in her purse to fix my hair, but it never worked. The comb had a tooth missing right in the middle. Anyway, for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money. They're using all these things to cover it up—like paying bills, or these fundraisers they talk about, or planning trips. It's all just a cover-up for where the money really went. So I just have to keep confronting them, you know? I have to keep asking them until they finally tell the truth. They think they can just distract me with all this talk about trips. I went on a trip to the beach once, and I found a perfect sand dollar, but it broke in my pocket on the way home. It just crumbled into dust.

opening_question.intent: Find out the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent, non-bizarre persecutory/theft-themed delusional belief that family and friends are hiding money, present for over 1 year. There are no confirmed hallucinations, thought insertion/broadcasting, negative symptoms, marked disorganization, manic symptoms, or broader schizophrenia-spectrum symptoms. Functioning appears relatively preserved aside from repeated confrontations about the delusional belief. This pattern is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder rather than paranoid schizophrenia.
